summary: Shardy is an MLIR-based tensor partitioning system whose SDY dialect binds per-tensor, per-dimension shardings to named logical meshes, with open and closed dimensions, explicitly replicated axes, sub-axes and priorities. A propagation pass infers unannotated shardings along per-op factor rules to a fixed point, resolving conflicts through user priorities, op priorities, aggressive and basic propagation; the SPMD partitioner that emits collectives is, short term, GSPMD's.
why_read: It is the current production sharding representation in the XLA/JAX stack and the documented successor of GSPMD's propagation.
main_contribution: An axis-based sharding representation with sub-axes, open/closed dimensions and priorities, plus a factor-based propagation algorithm with a four-level conflict resolution hierarchy and a compiler API for constraints, groups and manual computations.
main_limitation: Communication generation is delegated to the GSPMD partitioner and not described; propagation across meshes is not planned; the pages do not state how aggressive propagation picks among conflicting axes.
notes: Documentation, not a paper; five docs pages read (fetched 2026-11-07). No hardware is named, so target_hardware is empty although the catalog entry lists tpu-accelerator-mesh and multi-gpu-cluster.
